title: What if you painted your roof white? (15 s pipeline smoke test 2, not for posting)
formula: Scaled for 15 s: strange act + mocker -> time stamp + setback for him -> 'You see,' mechanism -> his comeuppance gag -> loop: now you're the one laughing
loop: Line 1: your neighbour laughs at your white roof. Last: now he's painting his roof white, and you're the one laughing.
facts: Light-coloured 'cool roofs' reflect more sunlight and stay much cooler than dark roofs in the sun; a dark roof absorbs it (US Department of Energy, Energy Saver: 'Cool Roofs'; verify wording before posting anything like this).
Shed, neighbour, ice cream and day 90: scenario framing.

lines.narration: You paint your shed roof white, and your neighbour *laughs*.
lines.scene: Cold open, sunny suburb: you on a step ladder, rolling white paint across your little shed's roof, half done. Over the fence, the neighbour (bowler hat) points and laughs beside his own shed with a black roof.
lines.camera: S1: low angle push-in on you, arc to include the laughing neighbour
lines.gag: The neighbour laughs so hard his bowler hat bounces

lines.scene: Same two sheds, wide, the sun now huge and white-hot; heat haze, the grass gone yellow.
lines.camera: S2: crane down from the blazing sun to the two sheds
lines.gag: The sun is so big it fills the top of the frame

lines.narration: You see, white bounces sunlight *away*. Black soaks it *up*.
lines.scene: Glowing sun rays hit your white roof and bounce back into the sky; the rays that hit his black roof sink in and it glows red-hot.
lines.camera: S3: side-on wide of both roofs, slow push
lines.gag: His black roof glows red like a stove

lines.narration: His ice cream doesn't stand a *chance*.
lines.scene: Hard cut: the neighbour in front of his shed, sweating, his face filling red, an ice cream cone melting in his hand.
lines.gag: The ice cream melts down to the cone; his face fills red

lines.narration: So now he's painting his roof white. And you're the one *laughing*.
lines.spoken: So now he's painting his roof white. [laughs] And you're the one laughing.
lines.scene: The neighbour on the ladder, painting his roof white; you in the foreground with a lemonade, laughing, his half-white roof behind you.
lines.camera: S5: push-in on you, end on the word
lines.gag: You raise your lemonade to him
